relations.note: Djedi proclaims that Ra fathered Ruddjedet’s three future royal children.
Djedi knows where knowledge associated with Thoth’s sanctuary is kept.

relations.myth: Nitocris gains underworld and jackal associations
relations.note: Fate/Grand Order associates Nitocris with Anubis through jackal imagery and underworld powers.

relations.myth: Nitocris gains magical Egyptian divine associations
relations.note: Fate/Grand Order associates Nitocris’s magical powers and pharaonic identity with Horus.
Setne witnesses the judgment system in which Ammit destroys condemned souls.
Setne hears Si-Osire address the Nubian envoy concerning Amun's power.
Setne witnesses Anubis participating in judgment beside Osiris.
Khaemwaset officiates in funerary rituals and burials for Apis as a divine manifestation.
Khaemwaset's statue bears a prayer to Atum.

relations.myth: Embedded contest of Egyptian and Nubian magicians
relations.note: Setne hears the embedded magician invoke Atum in an oath.
Tabubu identifies herself through her father's priestly service to Bastet; Setne never meets the goddess.

relations.myth: The Book of Thoth's second spell
relations.note: The book taken by Setne reveals Re with the Ennead, without personal dialogue.
Setne gives Harpocrates offerings beside Isis before searching the Coptos cemetery.
The historical Khaemwaset venerates Imhotep on a monument bearing the epithet son of Ptah.
Setne gives Isis an ox, goose, wine, burnt offering, and libation.

relations.myth: Ahwere's history of the divine book
relations.note: Ahwere invokes Neith's curse while addressing Setne, but he has no direct encounter with her.
Khaemwaset's statue bears a prayer to Osiris as an act of cultic devotion.

relations.myth: Journey through seven halls of Amenti
relations.note: Setne sees Osiris enthroned over judgment in Amenti.
Ptah's amulets and magical books restore or protect Setne during his struggle.
The historical Khaemwaset served as Ptah's sem-priest and high priest at Memphis.
Setne witnesses Thoth recording the weighing of the dead's deeds.

relations.myth: Theft of the Book of Thoth
relations.note: Setne removes the divine book belonging to Thoth from Naneferkaptah's tomb.
Sinuhe invokes Amun to bless Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Atum together with his Ennead to bless Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Hathor to love and sustain Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Horus to bless Senusret, whom the tale calls Horus who seizes.
Sinuhe praises Montu after killing the champion and later invokes him for Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Nut in the divine assembly blessing Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Ra as loving Senusret and inspiring worldwide fear of him.
Sinuhe invokes Sopdu as an eastern god of effective power.
Bata invokes sunrise as the divine forum revealing justice between the brothers.
The gods pity Bata and acknowledge that Anubis has avenged him.

relations.myth: Bata named Bull of the Ennead
relations.note: The assembled gods confer upon Bata the epithet Bull of the Ennead.
Khnum fashions a divinely beautiful wife for Bata at Re-Horakhty’s command.
A Jumilhac vignette depicts bull-form Bata carrying the mummy of Osiris.

relations.myth: Wenamun’s mission to obtain timber for Amun’s sacred bark
relations.note: Wenamun serves Amun’s institution, carries his dispatches, and claims the god commissioned and protected his mission.
